text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Smart-routing anomaly detected — region fallback loop between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu. High error spikes and retries observed. Auto-escalating to on-call.

sanjay: I’m getting pages for increased 5xxs on hosted API, looks tied to routing fallback. Can someone confirm region healthchecks?

emily: Confirmed, dashboards show probes failing in us-west, causing requests to reroute to eu, then eu failing and routing back to us-east, repeat. Latency and error rates spike every ~30s.

jess: Paging oncall, @sanjay you oncall? Also tagging infra. This started ~3m ago after the config push to routing-policy service.

ryan: I’m looking at the routing-policy logs now. There was a deploy at 1774508900 that changed the probe debounce and enabled aggressive cross-region fallback for lower latency. Could be the new policy triggering rapid flip.

ana_typo: sorry — meant @ana

ana: on it, checking healthcheck metrics and probe traces.

infra-bot: recent deploy 1774508899 by rli: "routing: enable aggressive cross-region fallback (debounce=2s)". Auto-rollback not enabled.

sanjay: Okay two immediate actions: 1) stop cross-region fallback to break the loop, 2) increase debounce/throttle on healthchecks. Who can flip policy?

emily: I can flip the routing policy to region-only (no cross-region fallback) via console. Doing it now — will set fallback to disabled for all tenants.

emily: done — routing fallback toggle set to false globally (api-call id: a1b2c3). Observability: routing churn stopped almost immediately. Error rate trending down.

ryan: While that bought us breathing room, we should revert the deploy that set debounce=2s. That probe is too aggressive and causing transient probes to mark regions unhealthy. Rolling back now.

ryan: rollback complete. New routing-policy revision matches previous stable config (debounce=10s).

ana: Healthchecks are stabilizing. us-west probe success rate back to 99% within 45s. eu also stable. No more rapid flapping in the last 2 minutes.

jess: Customer-impact check: SLO alerts in dashboards showed ~3.1% error rate for the hosted text API across the affected windows, peak error spike lasted ~6 minutes. Any targeted customers impacted?

ana: CS queue shows three active tickets referencing 503 errors from customers on multi-region routing. Two are high-volume PLG customers (ids redacted). We should reach out.

sanjay: Paging notes: Severity S2 (partial outage / degraded performance). Oncall: @sanjay handled mitigation. Handoff to morning shift @jess for post-incident cleanup and comms.

emily: Quick mitigation summary we’ll paste to status page later: 1) Disabled cross-region fallback, 2) Rolled back aggressive debounce change, 3) Scaled up us-east routing workers by +15% to clear backpressure.

ryan: Added temporary scaling: routing-workers from 40 -> 46 in us-east. Scaling back after backlog drained.

jess: Can we confirm there were no wrong model variants served as part of fallback? We had a separate report of a variant mismatch earlier this week.

ryan: Checked request logs — model variant routing was correct. The loop was purely healthcheck based. No incorrect model swaps.

ana: Running a quick customer impact tally: ~12k requests failed during the window, estimated <0.2% of daily traffic. Two PLG customers hit higher error rates for ~6 minutes; CSMs notified.

jess: Assigning follow-ups: 1) ENG-RUNTIME: add safety to disallow global aggressive fallback toggles without staged rollout — jira INF-1428 (owner: ryan). 2) ENG-PLATFORM: healthcheck canary thresholds and automated debounce lower bound — jira INF-1429 (owner: sanjay). 3) CS: proactive outreach to affected customers — jira CS-734 (owner: ana).

sanjay: Logging note: we should have more prominent alerting when routing churn > X per minute instead of just error rate. Filing INF-1430.

emily: Status page draft: "Intermittent errors for hosted inference due to routing policy configuration change resulting in a fallback loop. Mitigated by disabling cross-region fallback and rolling back the config. Full resolution in progress." Will post once we have final numbers.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT MITIGATED at 1774509730 — routing churn stopped, healthchecks stable, error rates declining. Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime.

jess: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open for handoff notes. I'll do the post-incident blameless writeup and coordinate the postmortem meeting.

ana: Leaving a note in the deploy: revert for rli's change and mark as revert reason "aggressive cross-region fallback caused healthcheck flips".

ryan: Also adding an integration test for routing policy that simulates transient probe failures to ensure debounce prevents oscillation.

sanjay: Handoff: @jess you now own the incident until final postmortem. ETA for postmortem doc: EOD tomorrow.

jess: Acknowledged. Will capture timeline, root cause (misconfigured debounce + global toggle), impact, and action items.

ana: Closing slack followups; will update CS tickets with customer notes and ETA for postmortem.

incident-bot: Thread auto-archived in 24h unless labeled "keep".
